content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn to make pot pies, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Watch a masterclass video on savory pastry techniques (45 minutes)
Step 2. Blind bake the bottom crust (20 minutes)
Step 3. Fill the pie crust with the prepared mixture (5 minutes)
Step 4. Sauté onions and celery in butter (10 minutes)
Step 5. Chop fresh parsley and thyme (5 minutes)
Step 6. Roll out the chilled dough on a floured surface (10 minutes)
Step 7. Trim the excess dough from the edges (2 minutes)
Step 8. Brush the top crust with an egg wash (3 minutes)
Step 9. Research different regional pot pie recipes (1 hour)
Step 10. Whisk in flour to create a roux (4 minutes)
Step 11. Peel and cube large russet potatoes (15 minutes)
Step 12. Blanch the cubed potatoes in boiling water (8 minutes)
Step 13. Shred a rotisserie chicken into bite-sized pieces (15 minutes)
Step 14. Mix flour and salt for the dough (5 minutes)
Step 15. Bake the assembled pot pie in the oven (45 minutes)
Step 16. Slowly pour in chicken stock while stirring (6 minutes)
Step 17. Clean the kitchen countertops (10 minutes)
Step 18. Simmer the sauce until thickened (12 minutes)
Step 19. Season the chicken with salt and pepper (2 minutes)
Step 20. Mix the herbs into the vegetable base (1 minute)
Step 21. Taste the filling and adjust seasoning (2 minutes)
Step 22. Incorporate cold butter into the flour mixture (8 minutes)
Step 23. Steam frozen peas until bright green (4 minutes)
Step 24. Add iced water to the dough until it holds together (5 minutes)
Step 25. Heat the heavy cream on the stove (3 minutes)
Step 26. Stir the cream into the thickened sauce (2 minutes)
Step 27. Allow the filling to cool to room temperature (30 minutes)
Step 28. Boil the potatoes until fork-tender (10 minutes)
Step 29. Purchase all necessary ingredients at the store (1 hour)
Step 30. Remove any skin or bones from the chicken (10 minutes)
Step 31. Drain and mash a portion of the potatoes for thickness (5 minutes)
Step 32. Fold the potatoes into the sauce (3 minutes)
Step 33. Melt unsalted butter in a large skillet (2 minutes)
Step 34. Sharpen the chef's knife (5 minutes)
Step 35. Sauté sliced carrots until tender (7 minutes)
Step 36. Dice the carrots and onions (12 minutes)
Step 37. Garnish the finished pie with remaining herbs (1 minute)
Step 38. Chill the dough in the refrigerator (1 hour)
Step 39. Measure out the frozen peas (1 minute)
Step 40. Deglaze the pan with a splash of white wine (2 minutes)
